base_prompt: Is a visible public deadline helpful for a personal creative project? Explain when accountability can become pressure. Aim for about 120 words.
text: A visible public deadline can help a personal creative project by turning a vague intention into a concrete commitment. Sharing a release date may encourage steady effort, reduce endless tinkering, and invite useful support from others. It works best when the scope is realistic, the timeline includes room for experimentation, and changing the date remains acceptable. Accountability becomes pressure when you start creating mainly to avoid embarrassment or disappointing an audience. Warning signs include sacrificing rest, hiding difficulties, rushing choices, or treating a missed deadline as proof of personal failure. For exploratory work, consider publicly committing to a progress update rather than a finished product. That preserves momentum while protecting the freedom to discover what the project needs.
